findings.reason: the control must say "two or more capturing groups" (or assert the message quotes the whole match rather than a group), otherwise the node's gate reports a guard that never fires.
findings.text: §3's second negative control says "a capturing group in the pattern fails the second case", but `deferred_work_terms` returns `re.findall` (reckon/doccheck.py:434-442) and a pattern with exactly ONE capture group makes `findall` return the group text as a string, not a tuple — measured at HEAD on the string "a follow-on and a follow-on": no group → `['follow-on', 'follow-on']` strings; one group `\b(follow)-ons?\b` → `['follow', 'follow']` (still strings); two groups `\b(follow)-(on)s?\b` → `[('follow', 'on'), ('follow', 'on')]` tuples; so a node that adds one group and runs the stated control sees the second case pass and records a control that proves nothing, which is exactly the fail-open shape the section exists to close

findings.reason: either name the surface the plan relies on (the MCP entry point or deployer that calls it) or drop the site and say so, because as written a node delivers and tests a guard on a dead function and calls the requirement met.
findings.text: §3 adds the prose refusal to `_append_comment` and spends case 3 and one control on it, but that function is reached by no production path: `reckon/mcp_edit_plan.py:137` defines it, `reckon/mcp.py:221` re-exports it, and the only callers are tests (`tests/test_mcp_tools.py:749,753`, `tests/test_plan_reads_stay_in_the_worktree.py:196`) — it is not registered as a FastMCP tool (mcp.py registers by `mcp.tool(name=...)`, and no such registration names it), so the guard is exercised only by the new test while nothing in the product writes a comment through it
